rules.structural_signal: testing isolated function logic with known inputs
rules.rationale: Parameterized tests cover multiple inputs efficiently with minimal code duplication

rules.structural_signal: pure function with no side effects and clear input output
rules.rationale: Pure functions are the ideal unit test target — complete isolation, deterministic results

rules.structural_signal: function with many edge cases on same signature
rules.rationale: Parameterized tests let you enumerate edge cases without repeating test logic

rules.structural_signal: combinatorial input space with tabular expected outputs
rules.rationale: Table-driven tests make combinatorial coverage explicit and easy to extend

rules.structural_signal: error handling paths and exception conditions
rules.rationale: Dedicated error path tests ensure graceful failure under invalid inputs

rules.structural_signal: async function or coroutine with await points
rules.rationale: Async code needs async-aware test runners to properly exercise await points and concurrency

rules.structural_signal: database queries or ORM operations against a real store
rules.rationale: Real database tests catch SQL/ORM bugs that mocks cannot detect

rules.structural_signal: REST or GraphQL endpoint handler with middleware
rules.rationale: API integration tests verify the full HTTP stack including middleware, serialization, and auth

rules.structural_signal: publish subscribe messaging or event-driven processing
rules.rationale: Message queue tests verify delivery semantics, ordering, and retry behavior

rules.structural_signal: third-party API client or external service dependency
rules.rationale: External service tests catch integration failures that mocks hide

rules.structural_signal: critical user journey through the full application
rules.rationale: Happy path E2E tests verify the primary user flow works end to end

rules.structural_signal: payment flow or revenue-critical business process
rules.rationale: Revenue-critical paths warrant the cost of E2E tests — failure here means lost money

rules.structural_signal: web application supporting multiple browsers
rules.rationale: Cross-browser tests catch rendering and API differences across browser engines

rules.structural_signal: microservice API consumed by multiple downstream services
rules.rationale: Consumer-driven contracts let teams deploy independently without breaking each other

rules.structural_signal: API provider verifying backward compatibility before deploy
rules.rationale: Provider verification catches breaking changes before they reach consumers

rules.structural_signal: serialization roundtrip or encoding decoding symmetry
rules.rationale: Property-based tests find edge cases in encoders/decoders that humans never think of

rules.structural_signal: stateful data structure with ordering or uniqueness invariants
rules.rationale: Invariant testing catches subtle state corruption after sequences of operations

rules.structural_signal: input space too large to enumerate but universal property exists
rules.rationale: Fuzzing explores the input space far more thoroughly than hand-written examples

rules.structural_signal: measuring test suite quality beyond code coverage
rules.rationale: Mutation testing objectively measures whether tests catch real bugs, not just execute code

rules.structural_signal: UI component rendering output stability
rules.rationale: Component snapshots catch unintended rendering changes with zero effort

rules.structural_signal: API response body format regression detection
rules.rationale: Response snapshots catch accidental field removal or type changes

rules.structural_signal: system exposed to sudden traffic spikes or viral load
rules.rationale: Spike tests reveal whether autoscaling and rate limiting handle sudden bursts

rules.structural_signal: long-running service suspected of memory leaks
rules.rationale: Soak tests find memory leaks and resource exhaustion invisible in short test runs

rules.structural_signal: finding system breaking point and maximum throughput
rules.rationale: Stress tests push beyond limits to find breaking points and verify graceful degradation

rules.structural_signal: verifying SLA compliance under expected load
rules.rationale: Capacity tests determine maximum throughput while meeting latency SLAs

rules.structural_signal: source code handling user input with potential injection
rules.rationale: Static analysis catches injection vulnerabilities before code runs

rules.structural_signal: running web application needing runtime vulnerability scan
rules.rationale: Dynamic scanning finds exploitable vulnerabilities in running applications

rules.structural_signal: third-party dependencies needing CVE monitoring
rules.rationale: Dependency scanning is low-cost high-value — catches known vulnerabilities automatically

rules.structural_signal: public web application requiring WCAG compliance
rules.rationale: Automated WCAG checks catch the most common accessibility violations

rules.structural_signal: CSS refactoring or design system component visual consistency
rules.rationale: Pixel diff catches subtle visual regressions that functional tests miss

rules.structural_signal: OpenAPI schema defined for API contract compliance
rules.rationale: Schema validation is fast and automated when a formal spec exists

rules.structural_signal: state-changing API endpoint that must be safely retried
rules.rationale: Idempotency tests prevent duplicate processing bugs that are hard to debug in production

rules.structural_signal: LLM agent with versioned prompts being iterated
rules.rationale: Prompt regression is the first test every agent needs — without it, prompt changes are blind

rules.structural_signal: agent with multiple tools and function calling capability
rules.rationale: Tool call validation catches the most common agent failure: calling the wrong tool with wrong params

rules.structural_signal: conversational agent maintaining state across turns
rules.rationale: Multi-turn tests catch amnesia and self-contradiction that erode user trust

rules.structural_signal: RAG agent that must ground answers in provided documents
rules.rationale: Hallucination detection is critical for any agent making factual claims from sources

rules.structural_signal: agent used in automated pipeline where output is parsed by code
rules.rationale: Downstream code breaks on variance — determinism testing quantifies reliability

rules.structural_signal: agent with large context injection approaching token limits
rules.rationale: Token budget tests prevent silent truncation and control API costs

rules.structural_signal: public-facing AI agent needing content safety guardrails
rules.rationale: Safety testing is non-negotiable for user-facing agents — failure is a liability

rules.structural_signal: multi-agent pipeline with sequential handoffs between agents
rules.rationale: Chain tests verify data flows correctly and errors propagate gracefully across agents

rules.structural_signal: agent responses streamed via SSE or WebSocket to client
rules.rationale: Stream validation catches chunk corruption and incomplete responses that batch tests miss

rules.structural_signal: agent with response time SLA or latency-sensitive interaction
rules.rationale: Latency profiling establishes baselines and detects performance regressions

rules.structural_signal: agent handling long conversations near context window capacity
rules.rationale: Context window tests verify graceful degradation as history grows

rules.structural_signal: RAG agent providing citations that must reference real sources
rules.rationale: Grounding tests verify the citation chain — claims must trace back to real sources

rules.structural_signal: rate-limited API endpoint with quota enforcement
rules.rationale: Rate limit tests verify abuse prevention and multi-tenant resource isolation
